sources.note: Not fetched: HTTP 403 to automated retrieval. Its ratios are quoted here from the sites that reproduce its table (named per figure).

published.note: Mast, forestay, centreboard and rudder are class-rule dimensions from the transom's measurement point, turned into distances from the stem with the rule's hull length (4.70 m ± 0.01). No source gives her waterline beam, canoe-body draft, coefficients or a polar.

figures.label: Main, with roach
figures.roundTrip: the roach is set so the main is the class's 9.12 m² (½·5.75·2.65 = 7.619 m²)

figures.label: Hull speed
figures.work: 1.34·√(4.4/0.3048) = 5.091, worked here from the class's waterline

figures.label: Draft, board down
figures.roundTrip: the board's span is solved so that the draft reaches 0.97 m; the rule's board, its leading edge vertical, reaches 0.92 m below the hull

mastAftOfStem.how: the middle of where the rule lets the mast's front be at the deck: inside the partner (1.510–1.710 m aft of the stem) with the 65–75 mm section, 1.525–1.625

keelLeAftOfStem.how: the pivot 2650 mm from the transom's datum, 85–95 mm aft of the leading edge, the leading edge taken vertical (the down angle is the sailor's)

balance.why: Her rig and foils are fixed by class rule to within 0.05 m, the best positions in the fleet. But no lead band is quoted for a centreboard dinghy with a trapeze crew, whose balance is trimmed by rake, board angle and heel, and her hull (BWL, Tc, displacement with crew) is estimated throughout.

values.value: 3.66 m² (Heron's formula on the rule's maximum luff 4100, leech 3750, foot 1955)

disagreements.used: LP 1.78 m, from the rule's edges

published.estimatedWhy: BWL is 0.81 of the beam, the Laser's proportion in Day (2017); Tc is what the synthetic hull then needs to float 250 kg (the rule's 120 kg boat and an estimated 130 kg crew). Freeboard, I and BAS go through a hull depth read off a sketch. The board's span is solved to the published draft and its leading edge is taken vertical; the rudder hangs from the waterline, 0.58 m of its blade below it.
